segments.t: korTTY is a modular JavaFX SSH client built on a layered architecture. This guide describes the core modules, their responsibilities, dependencies, and how they interact to deliver a seamless terminal experience with advanced features like job scheduling, AI integration, and terminal effect plugins.
The following diagram shows the main components of korTTY and how they relate:
KorTTY is organized into distinct functional modules. The diagram below groups them by function:
SSH connectivity, shared interactive host-key trust, session management, AI integration, terminal automation
Signed model/prompt catalog, Hugging Face metadata/downloads, embedded llama.cpp and MLX runtimes, and signed runtime packages
KTPH000, KTPH001, KTPH002, KTPH003, KTPH004, KTPH005
Safe source scanning, extraction, chunking, embeddings, vector stores, synchronization, and bounded retrieval
JavaFX user interface, dialogs, terminal views, SFTP manager
Domain objects for connections, credentials, snippets, jobs
XML serialization, file I/O, repository pattern
Activity-aware sleep and App Nap management per platform
Default-off local control API: transport, token, verbs, event bus (see KTPH000Control APIKTPH001)
The KTPH000 client that speaks the control API (see KTPH001Control CLIKTPH002)
Coding-agent awareness: detects terminal coding agents in panes, tracks their state, and feeds the Coding Agents panel and notifications
Session isolation levels and the sandboxed local shells; SSH sessions run in session worker processes (KTPH000)
KTPH000, KTPH001, KTPH002, KTPH003, KTPH004, KTPH005
Paste protection: inspects pasted text and decides whether to confirm, sanitize or pace it
Enterprise policy file (KTPH000): managed settings, restrictions and encrypted policy values
Shell integration (prompt marks, command status, notifications) and per-pane activity tracking
Opt-in UI timing trace for performance work
Platform support for packaged builds, such as Flatpak
KorTTY uses KTPH000SithTermFX 1.2.7KTPH001 as its primary terminal emulator, built from source during the build process. SithTermFX provides:
KTPH000Terminal emulationKTPH001: VT100/xterm-compatible terminal rendering powered by a custom JavaFX control

KTPH062OSC 8 hyperlinksKTPH063: Clickable explicit hyperlinks printed by programs. korTTY replaces SithTermFX's default link handler in every pane with its own allowlist (KTPH000, KTPH001, KTPH002, KTPH003, KTPH004, strictly parsed, at most 8 KB, no control or bidi characters, KTPH005 limited to recipients, subject, body and in-reply-to) and opens links through JavaFX KTPH006. Links open only on a single, still Cmd/Ctrl+click without Alt (KTPH007, user decision D2). korTTY's settings provider answers SithTermFX's KTPH008 with that rule, and SithTermFX 1.2.3 follows an OSC 8 link only on a still, single primary click the rule accepts, so a plain click, a double or triple click and a drag release on a link act as on other text, word and line selection included. The KTPH009 that SithTermFX then navigates hands itself to its pane (KTPH010), which opens it only when the primary KTPH011 filter that KTPH012 installs on the canvas noted that same click, with the gesture, on that same link, so the gesture holds under any settings provider and no navigation bypasses the checks below. The same filter opens a link korTTY found in plain text itself, by a pure decision table, and consumes that click with a focus request, so the split pane still tracks the focused pane. KTPH013 and other targets stay plain text, and a KTPH014 target becomes a link only in a pane that opens files as text (see below), so terminal output never reaches KTPH015 and cannot launch a local file. Panes keep SithTermFX's default KTPH016 mode, in which linked text keeps its own colors and attributes, including SGR changes inside the link (since SithTermFX 1.2.3), and is underlined while the gesture is held over it, and KTPH017 records a link cell with KTPH018, the style of the text beneath the link. korTTY registers no SithTermFX KTPH019: links in plain text are found on demand instead, so they cost nothing while output arrives and open only through korTTY's gate; KTPH020 fails the build if a filter is added. KTPH021 is the click policy's hit resolver: under the buffer lock it returns the OSC 8 link of the clicked cell, or else runs KTPH022 for web and e-mail addresses over the logical line around the cell, bounded to ±16 wrapped rows and 4096 characters, and drops a token that may run on past that window instead of opening it cut short. The kinds come from a per-pane supplier that reads KTPH023 on every click, so detection costs nothing while output arrives. KTPH024 resolves the same way only when the mouse reaches another cell: a KTPH025 handler added after SithTermFX's own sets the canvas cursor explicitly on every cell change (HAND only for a link that can open), draws the underline of a plain-text link as KTPH026s in the pane's KTPH027 layer (KTPH028, an unmanaged, mouse-transparent KTPH029 in the pane wrapper at a negative view order, placed through scene coordinates because the wrapper also holds the timestamp gutter and the agent panel) and shows a tooltip with KTPH030 (punycode host, percent-encoded controls and bidi characters, shortened to about 200 characters without cutting the host). It tears down on exit, drag, scroll, non-modifier key, pane or window focus loss and scene removal, and while a link is shown it follows a buffer model listener (coalesced onto the FX thread) and canvas resizes to re-resolve. An OSC 8 click whose visible text is a URL on another host than the target (KTPH031) opens only after KTPH032, asked after the click is handled, with Cancel as the default button. The terminal context menu reaches the same links without a modifier: KTPH033 adds a canvas KTPH034 filter that resolves the link under every right-button press (any other press forgets it), and KTPH035 puts KTPH064Open LinkKTPH065 (the click's open path, mismatch question included) and KTPH066Copy Link AddressKTPH067 (through KTPH036, so the internal clipboard mode applies; an OSC 8 link's KTPH037 target, a plain-text address as printed) above the edit entries for a link with a target. Files go the same ways without a browser: KTPH038 is a path the detector found (KTPH039, split by KTPH040) or an OSC 8 KTPH041 target that KTPH042 accepts (absolute path, no KTPH043 network share, no backslash, no control, bidi or format characters after decoding, a host without user name or port). KTPH044 creates a KTPH045 link only while the pane's KTPH046 is enabled (asked on the emulator thread), which KTPH047 makes true only for SSH and local-shell panes while a KTPH048 is set, and KTPH049 sets one only when the policy's KTPH050 is not KTPH051; the same condition adds KTPH052 to the pane's plain-text link kinds. The pane's shared lookup drops the file of a link the handler does not accept (an OSC 8 host that is not empty, KTPH053, the connection host, the prompt host or the local host name, by first DNS label), so the hover, the click and the context menu agree. Opening resolves the path with KTPH054 / KTPH055 (absolute, KTPH056, and relative against the working directory at click time, which is looked up only for a relative path; UNC and device paths refused before and after resolving) and reads it through the same reader as KTPH068Open in Snippet EditorKTPH069, with the foreign-session guard, regular-file and UTF-8 checks and a 10 MB cap for SFTP and local reads that also stops a file growing during the read. A file from an OSC 8 link opens read-only: KTPH057 gets no overwrite or save-as action and a KTPH058. KTPH059 adds its KTPH060 handler from KTPH061, after SithTermFX adds its own there, so the cursor korTTY sets wins also over an OSC 8 link it does not open.

KTPH028Quick selectKTPH029: KTPH030Edit → Quick SelectKTPH031 (Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+Space) labels what the focused pane shows. The chord is a KTPH000 constant routed through the scene shortcut router (scope: a terminal tab with the keyboard focus inside it; residue: space or NUL) and set on the menu item, which is disabled outside terminal tabs. KTPH001 reads the visible rows at the panel's scroll origin under the buffer lock, joins wrapped rows within the viewport (sliced to the detector's 16 KB input cap) and runs KTPH002 for every kind, dropping a token that runs on past the viewport; the user's own patterns (KTPH003, from KTPH004: at most 16 of at most 512 characters, compiled once per change of the list) run over the same scanned text and come out as KTPH005, each through a KTPH006 with 10 ms per line and 100 ms for all of one capture, a pattern that overruns being skipped for the rest of the capture, and a pattern match replaces the built-in matches it overlaps when it is at least as long as each of them; KTPH007 assigns prefix-free labels from the user's alphabet (KTPH008, validated by KTPH009, the default when unusable; one letter per text up to the alphabet's size, otherwise two) bottom row first, one per distinct text; KTPH010 is a pure state machine over KTPH011 and Shift (modifier keys and the starting chord are ignored, a label copies, Shift on its last letter opens, Backspace edits the prefix, Escape and any other key cancel). KTPH012 installs the split pane's first KTPH013, KTPH014 and KTPH015 filters (before KTPH016's own, so before the agent input lock and the per-pane broadcast mirror): while a session runs every key, typed character and input-method event is consumed, and KTPH017 reuses KTPH018 to swallow the last key's KTPH019 once plus any input-method text until the next key press. It draws KTPH020 boxes and inline-styled KTPH021 chips (pane colors inverted, terminal font) into the pane's KTPH022 layer through scene coordinates (KTPH023), copies through KTPH024, opens a URL, an e-mail address or, where the pane opens files (KTPH025), a path through the widget's KTPH026 (the Cmd/Ctrl+click path) and copies whatever it does not open, and ends on a mouse press, canvas focus loss, a canvas move or resize, a scroll-bar change, a font-size change (KTPH027) or scene removal; a buffer model listener, coalesced onto the FX thread, drops the matches whose cells no longer hold their captured text and ends the session when none is left.
KTPH000Session integrationKTPH001: Direct JAXB marshaling of terminal state for session recording and replay
KTPH000Color supportKTPH001: Configurable ANSI and TrueColor handling with per-connection overrides

KTPH010Scrollback memory limit and compressionKTPH011: Since SithTermFX 1.2.6 a pane's history is bounded by an estimate of its heap as well as by its line count. KTPH000 answers KTPH001 and KTPH002 from KTPH003 and KTPH004, and KTPH005 hands a saved change to every open pane's KTPH006. With compression on, a low-priority SithTermFX thread packs history lines into deflated blocks of up to 128 lines once a pane has had no output for 1.5 s, holding the buffer lock for a few milliseconds at a time; the rows on screen with a screenful around them, the newest screenful and lines with a custom highlighting stay unpacked, and nothing is packed while find results are shown. A packed line keeps its KTPH007 identity, wrapped flag and styles, so KTPH008, the command marks and the keyword highlighter, which all anchor on line identity, are unaffected; drawing a line or reading its entries unpacks its block, KTPH009 decodes without unpacking

KTPH003Hyperlink boundary fixKTPH004: Hyperlink hit-testing rejects the non-existent row at KTPH000, preventing bottom-row KTPH001 range errors. korTTY carried this as a pinned patch until it shipped upstream in SithTermFX 1.2.3; KTPH002 pins the behaviour

KTPH005Shortcut-chord fixKTPH006: Shortcut-chord KTPH000 characters (for example KTPH007KTPH002KTPH008+KTPH009KTPH003KTPH010+KTPH011KTPH004KTPH012) no longer reach the pty or broadcast panes. Carried as a korTTY patch until SithTermFX 1.2.3; KTPH001 pins the behaviour

KTPH005Control-sequence bounds fixKTPH006: The 1024-character push-back through which KTPH000 re-reads the characters it cannot place in a CSI ahead of the sequence is bounded: stray characters and then whole parameters that do not fit are dropped, and the re-emitted sequence always keeps its final character, so an overlong sequence in remote output no longer throws KTPH001 on the emulator thread and ends the session. KTPH002 replays the same stray characters. Carried as a korTTY patch until it shipped upstream in SithTermFX 1.2.3 (KTPH003); KTPH004 pins the behaviour

KTPH000Scroll-region correctnessKTPH001: The scrolling region does not confine the cursor while origin mode (DECOM) is off. Text addressed above the top margin or below the bottom one stays on that line instead of being pulled into the region, and only a line feed or autowrap that actually crosses the bottom margin scrolls — so tmux's first pane row, its status line and the cursor all land where the application put them. Carried as a korTTY patch until it shipped upstream in SithTermFX 1.2.2
Clones SithTermFX at tag KTPH000 into KTPH001 (no GitHub token required)
Builds it locally using Maven via the KTPH000 task — the released tag as is, since korTTY carries no SithTermFX patches
Installs artifacts to the local Maven repo (KTPH000); the task runs again whenever the core or UI JAR of the pinned version is missing there
Links SithTermFX core and UI modules into the korTTY JAR
No network access is needed after cloning; all build steps are deterministic and reproducible.

KorTTY stores its main configuration, credentials, and session state under KTPH000, primarily as JAXB XML. Local-model registration also uses JAXB XML, while knowledge-store configuration is strict JSON and the local vector graph is a regenerable binary snapshot. This approach ensures:
KTPH000PortabilityKTPH001: Easy manual inspection and migration across systems
KTPH000EncryptionKTPH001: Sensitive data (passwords, SSH key passphrases, master password hash) is encrypted with AES-256-GCM
KTPH000Atomic writesKTPH001: File updates use temporary files and atomic rename to prevent corruption on crash
KTPH000No required databaseKTPH001: Local HNSW is self-contained; Qdrant is an optional second vector backend
KTPH000JAXB MarshalingKTPH001 converts domain objects to/from XML with automatic schema validation. Key repositories include:
KTPH000: Manages KTPH001 objects with SFTP, jump server, and tunnel details
KTPH000: Wraps imported SSH keys with encrypted passphrases
KTPH000: Persists KTPH001 objects and the execution journal
Master password is hashed once on first login, stored as KTPH000
All encrypted fields use AES-256-GCM with random IVs, under a key derived from the master password
SSH key passphrases, connection passwords, and sudo secrets are encrypted before persistence
Backup archives can be encrypted with password-protected ZIP or GPG
Apache SSHD terminal connection of one pane: jump host, authentication, shell channel and disconnect detection
Live list of the open SSH and Mosh terminal connections (one per pane), read by the JMX MBean

The SSH tunnels (KTPH000, KTPH001, KTPH002) of one terminal tab: opened on the tab's first SSH session after login, stopped before a reconnect and opened again afterwards, moved to another pane of the same server when that pane closes; split panes never open their own
One-time confirmation per connection and tunnel set before tunnels open, stored as a fingerprint in KTPH000
Shares normalized host:port TOFU pins across interactive Terminal, SFTP, and Mosh bootstrap connections with atomic, cross-process persistence
Centralized SSH key storage with encrypted passphrase support
Mosh protocol connector using the mosh4j library (dynamically loaded)
Manages AI chat sessions and conversation history
Maps a profile to HTTP, Anthropic, local CLI, or embedded llama.cpp transport, then adds prompt presets and optional RAG
Returns a reverified cache/bootstrap immediately and schedules one signed stable-channel refresh for recommendations and preset-family mappings
Shares one isolated authenticated sidecar per compatible GGUF configuration and grants reference-counted request leases
Retrieves bounded excerpts for ordinary AI actions and adds the untrusted context before the model preset
Executes agent workflows: probes SSH session, sends task to model, validates/executes commands
Configures web tools (Tavily, Brave Search, SearXNG, etc.) per profile
Exports AI chats to Markdown, PDF, YAML, JSON, XML, Asciidoctor
Main scheduler service; manages scheduled jobs and execution queue
Executes individual jobs (SSH command, script, AI agent, SFTP, Rsync)

KTPH000First LaunchKTPH001: User creates a master password (minimum 6 characters, strength-checked via zxcvbn)
KTPH001StorageKTPH002: Password is hashed using PBKDF2 with 310,000 iterations and stored in KTPH000
KTPH000UnlockingKTPH001: Master password unlocks all encrypted data (connection passwords, SSH key passphrases, credentials, backup archive passwords)
KTPH000EncryptionKTPH001: AES-256-GCM with random IVs; encryption/decryption happens on-demand when accessing sensitive fields

KTPH000Interactive Terminal/SFTP/Mosh bootstrapKTPH001: One shared TOFU verifier is keyed by normalized host name and port. First use shows the OpenSSH SHA-256 fingerprint with KTPH002NoKTPH003 as the default; an exact match is silent, while a changed key is hard-blocked without retry. Only a connection the user opened in a terminal tab or the SFTP manager may replace a changed key, after an explicit fingerprint confirmation and as a compare-and-swap against the reviewed key; background callers build their verifier with the never-replace policy.

KTPH002Interactive storageKTPH003: KTPH000 stores public-key material through an atomic replacement guarded by both in-process and cross-process locks. Its transient KTPH001 companion is not backed up.

KTPH001JobSchedulerKTPH002: Unattended SSH, SFTP, and Rsync use separate connection-ID-based pins in KTPH000, including OpenSSH public-key material needed by Rsync. A per-job override can disable that verification only when the risk is explicitly accepted.
KTPH000Environment-specificKTPH001: Credentials can be scoped to Production, Development, Test, or Staging
KTPH002Glob patternsKTPH003: Server patterns like KTPH000 or KTPH001 automatically match connections
KTPH000Stored encryptedKTPH001: All credential passwords use AES-256-GCM
Each embedded model process binds only to KTPH000 on a random port and requires a generated API key stored in an owner-only temporary file.
The fixed llama.cpp launch command enables offline mode and disables the web UI, agent, UI MCP proxy, and slots endpoint; inherited KTPH000 and Hugging Face token variables are removed.
Hugging Face tokens and AI profile API keys are encrypted with the master password. Model downloads are pinned to an immutable revision and verified with SHA-256.

RAG accepts only centrally allowlisted, content-validated text. Retrieved excerpts are bounded and wrapped as explicitly untrusted data so indexed instructions cannot replace korTTY's system/action contract.
Runtime update indexes are verified as exact bytes with Ed25519 before package URLs are parsed; packages also have signed size/SHA-256 metadata and safe ZIP extraction limits.

Runtime withdrawals are persisted before process shutdown through a runtime-root denylist plus package marker. Active pointers and unsafe rollback-history entries are removed, registered models are rebound to a non-executable quarantine marker, and the launch path rechecks the marker so stale registry state cannot revive a withdrawn binary.

A package that passes the lightweight version health check remains pending until its first real GGUF-backed authenticated API start. KTPH000 confirms it on readiness or restores the newest healthy non-revoked installation and model bindings after a start failure.

The independent model/prompt catalog has its own Ed25519 trust root and strict schema. Its cache is reverified before use; a missing key disables both cache trust and network refresh and selects the compiled bootstrap.
Remote Qdrant uses HTTPS, with plain HTTP restricted to a loopback test/local service.

KTPH000mosh4jKTPH001: Its five SHA-256-pinned, architecture-specific release JARs and protobuf are bundled in native builds and dynamically loaded only when Mosh is needed. The child loader reuses Bouncy Castle from the application parent instead of shipping a second copy.
KTPH000rsync / sshKTPH001: External commands used by JobScheduler Rsync jobs
KTPH000ffmpegKTPH001: Optional; used for terminal recording video export

KTPH001llama.cpp runtimeKTPH002: Downloaded independently under KTPH000; CPU packages cover every supported platform, Metal is available on macOS, and Vulkan is available for supported Windows/Linux targets. It is never folded into the base installer.
KTPH000QdrantKTPH001: Optional external vector service. Remote endpoints require HTTPS; HTTP is loopback-only. Local HNSW is dependency-free and remains the default knowledge-store backend.
KTPH000SithTermFX buildKTPH001: Cloned and built locally (Maven); its accidentally published JUnit dependency is excluded from the runtime.

KTPH000Browser assetsKTPH001: An isolated, pinned Node.js is used only at build time for Monaco and for JavaFX-WebKit compatibility processing of the SHA-256-pinned Mermaid bundle. Monaco's editor and diff pages share one mode-aware IIFE/CSS pair while retaining all five workers and language services. Mermaid and MathJax remain separate lazy resources; Prettier Standalone with five selected plugins and the sql-formatter UMD build run without Node at runtime.

KTPH000External formatter payloadKTPH001: Only shfmt, Perl::Tidy and their manifest are staged beside the app; the logo video is stored once per source surface as H.264/yuv420p at 640×360 without audio.

KTPH002Clean native stagingKTPH003: KTPH000 uses a final Gradle KTPH001, so obsolete dependencies, formatter trees and Mosh architectures are deleted. Bouncy Castle is deduplicated, and JNA, pty4j, zstd-jni and jSerialComm are repacked with only the current target's native paths and binary architecture.

KTPH002Native packaging and gatesKTPH003: The selected Gradle JDK 25 toolchain supplies KTPH000 for .app/.dmg, .exe/.msi, .deb and .rpm output. KTPH001 emits JSON/Markdown component reports and CI enforces the committed release comparison, at least 10% installer reduction, absolute app/DMG limits and frozen verified-size budgets with 2% tolerance.

KTPH002JavaFX dependency alignmentKTPH003: KTPH000 checks every resolved compile, runtime and test classpath before compilation and packaging. Standard OpenJFX modules must remain at 21.0.12; only the compile-time KTPH001 bridge uses its separately pinned version, and it may not enter a runtime classpath.

KTPH004llama.cpp runtime packagingKTPH005: Separate Gradle tasks verify the pinned upstream tag/commit/archive SHA-256, build only KTPH000 plus required shared libraries, stage a backend-specific tree, and produce a reproducible immutable ZIP and signed-index descriptor input. The weekly runtime workflow opens candidate PRs; a scope job runs the full platform/backend matrix only when the pin file, the workflow, or the llama Java sources changed (a KTPH001-only change gets a single smoke leg); every built leg runs a native link smoke, the reference package runs the full authenticated chat/embedding/JSON/sleep/parallel-sidecar contract, and a protected KTPH002 environment with required reviewers gates manual stable promotion from KTPH003.

KTPH002Model/prompt catalog promotionKTPH003: A separate manual KTPH000-only workflow validates the canonical strict-schema JSON, requires a sequence greater than the latest immutable release, runs schema/trust-chain tests, matches the signing key to the application trust root, signs the exact bytes, and publishes through the reviewer-protected KTPH001 environment without a preview channel.
KTPH001Compile-timeKTPH002: On JDK 25 the JavaFX KTPH000 artifact is supplied on the upgrade module path so WebView bridges compile consistently; the module is absent from JDK 26.

KTPH003Packaging-timeKTPH004: Gradle resolves and invokes the same Temurin JDK 25 toolchain used for compilation, so the trimmed runtime contains KTPH000 even when the system KTPH001/KTPH002 is newer.
KTPH002Module pathKTPH003: JavaFX, SithTermFX and Apache SSHD are available during compilation; unused KTPH000 and KTPH001 are not included in the packaged runtime.
KTPH001Log fileKTPH002: KTPH000, rolled over daily, with the log directory and retention set under KTPH003Settings → LoggingKTPH004 (SLF4J with Logback backend)
KTPH002JMX monitoringKTPH003: MBean KTPH000 exposes the live SSH and Mosh terminal connections (each split pane counts, local shells do not), memory and uptime; KTPH001 is not tracked and stays 0
KTPH000JobScheduler journalKTPH001: Detailed execution logs with configurable retention (14 days default, unlimited if set to 0)

KTPH001Project screen snapshotsKTPH002: The last visible screen of each terminal tab of a saved project, gzip-compressed in KTPH000 and shown locally (never sent to the server) when the project is reopened with Auto-Reconnect

KTPH000UI ThreadKTPH001: JavaFX application thread handles all rendering and user interaction
KTPH000SSH Session ThreadsKTPH001: One thread per active SSH connection (Apache SSHD pool)

KTPH000Split-connection handshakeKTPH001: Same-server and newly selected split connections perform network setup on a worker while a JavaFX progress dialog keeps host-key and keyboard-interactive prompts responsive.
KTPH000Job Executor ThreadsKTPH001: Background thread pool for JobScheduler execution
KTPH000AI Chat ThreadsKTPH001: Background threads for API requests (non-blocking UI)
KTPH000AI catalog refreshKTPH001: The first catalog consumer gets verified cache/bootstrap data immediately and starts at most one background stable-channel refresh.

KTPH000Local-model provisioningKTPH001: Setup-assistant metadata inspection, signed runtime installation, resumable GGUF download/verification, registration, and real chat/embedding tests run on background futures; JavaFX receives only progress and final state updates. Text/Coding/RAG assignments are persisted after every selected model passes.

KTPH000llama.cpp sidecarsKTPH001: One native process per compatible loaded GGUF configuration; different models can load and generate concurrently, while leases keep active requests from being stopped. Runtime-configuration saves first request an idle stop and are rejected while a lease is busy.

KTPH000RAG workersKTPH001: Source previews, extraction, embedding batches, and HNSW candidate builds run outside the JavaFX thread; a daemon WatchService thread debounces automatic source changes. The pane permits only one active scan/index operation and returns the reviewed preview to JavaFX before configuration or indexing changes.

KTPH000RAG coordinatorKTPH001: One serialized worker and watcher per store prevents overlapping writes, reconciles Automatic sources during application startup independently of credential/JobScheduler startup, persists source hashes/counts/status, and reloads UI state after completion.
KTPH000File I/O ThreadsKTPH001: Async writes for history, journal, and recordings

KTPH000Web formatter requestsKTPH001: Background callers are serialized with one total timeout; creation, loading and invocation of the lazy Prettier/SQL WebView remain confined to the JavaFX application thread, and failures discard the engine generation.

KTPH001Mermaid render requestsKTPH002: Background callers receive KTPH000 results while all access to the single lazy renderer WebView stays on the JavaFX application thread. Requests are serialized; cancellation, a 30-second timeout, or a WebEngine error discards the engine generation, and idle cleanup releases the hidden WebView.
